factsheet_lines_1_indexed.3: 1. Isabelle Chang - Lead demonstrator and escort for government officials during the Ring of Silence Protocol pilot test.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.4: 2. Nouvelle Genève Environmental Coalition - The group of environmental scientists involved in the development of the protocol.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.5: 3. Council of Spiritual Leaders - Collaborative group of spiritual leaders who contributed to the creation of "Soul Harmony."
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.6: 4. Lake Ypsilon Community - The first community where the Ring of Silence Protocol was piloted.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.7: 5. Global Urban Planning Forum - An international body interested in adopting the protocol in various cities.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.8: 6. Ethical Convention on Acoustic Innovations - A gathering established to discuss and regulate the ethical implications of new technologies like Soul Harmony.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.12: 1. Development of the Ring of Silence Protocol (2046) - Initiated by environmental scientists and spiritual leaders in Nouvelle Genève.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.13: 2. Establishment of the sound-absorbing moat around Lake Ypsilon - The first implementation of the protocol for testing purposes.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.14: 3. Demonstration by Isabelle Chang - A guided meditative walk for government officials to showcase the protocol's effectiveness.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.15: 4. Global adoption of the Ring of Silence Protocol - Cities worldwide begin to implement the protocol to enhance urban living conditions.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.16: 5. Debate over Soul Harmony's potential misuse - Concerns raised about the technology's ability to influence human psychology.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.17: 6. Ethical Conventions of 2047 - Meetings held to create guidelines ensuring the protocol's use respects individual freedoms.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.21: 1. Nouvelle Genève - The city where the Ring of Silence Protocol was developed.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.22: 2. Lake Ypsilon - The site of the first pilot test for the protocol.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.23: 3. Various global metropolises - Cities that showed interest in adopting the protocol.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.24: 4. International Convention Centers - Venues for the 2047 ethical conventions.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.28: 1. 2046 - The year the Ring of Silence Protocol was developed and piloted.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.29: 2. 2047 - The year ethical conventions were held to address concerns about the protocol.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.33: 1. Urban Noise Pollution - Increasing levels of noise in cities prompted the need for innovative solutions.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.34: 2. Integration of Science and Spirituality - Combining acoustic engineering with psychological principles led to the creation of Soul Harmony.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.35: 3. Desire for Holistic Urban Living - Cities sought methods to improve quality of life through innovative urban planning.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.36: 4. Concerns of Mind Control - The psychological influence of Soul Harmony raised ethical questions about its use, necessitating regulation.
factsheet_lines_1_indexed.37: 5. Global Interest in Sustainable Innovations - The successful pilot in Nouvelle Genève sparked international curiosity in sustainable urban solutions.

items.instruction: Under the confirmation rules a preserved unit (assertion_only or conflict_flagged) must be its own group, and that group's statement must be the unit's source_statement copied verbatim, with no added or removed punctuation. Fix it in one of two ways. (a) Only for assertion_only: if an exact factsheet line supports the assertion as stated, set status "grounded", give the exact line(s) as evidence, and say why in "note". The unit may then stay in its group. (b) Otherwise give the unit its own group: a new id ground-<event>-<nn> with an unused nn, source_unit_ids [the unit], statement = source_statement verbatim, and a grouping_rationale. Remaining members keep their group. Every distinct answer label of every group must have exactly one source_qa record with two closed-book questions (AUTHORING-SPEC.md). Move, keep or write source_qa records so this holds, with unit_id set to the record's group id.
